To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degradation of lindane (a highly toxic pesticide), methyl parathon (a moderately toxic pesticide), and carbofuron (an insecticide), by bacterial isolates, is enhanced in a mixed culture, under anaerobic conditions, and that a specific pesticide-enriched bacterial culture is more effective than a mixed pesticide-enriched one.
a mixed pesticide-enriched bacterial culture is more effective for multi-pesticide biodegradation.
a specific pesticide-enriched bacterial culture showed maximum degradation in a facultative condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biodegradation potential of different enriched cultures of bacteria under different environmental conditions and also the degradation of multi-pesticides by mixed pesticide-enriched cultures.
the degradation of multi-pesticides by enriched bacterial cultures.

the degradation of lindane (a highly persistent pesticide), methyl parathions (one of the most toxic organophosphate pesticides) and carbofurans (one of the highly toxic insecticides) by different enriched bacterial cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the degradation of a pesticide depends on the type of the culture, the type of the pesticide, environmental conditions and the type of the interaction between the pesticide and the culture.
a mixed pesticide-enriched consortium would be a better option than the specific pesticide-enriched cultures for the bioremediation purpose.
the degradation of pesticides is a complex phenomenon and the degradation potential of different bacterial cultures varies with pesticides and environmental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a bacterial consortium, which is enriched with the mixture of all possible pesticides present at the site, seems to be a more effective option for the effective remediation of multi-pesticides contaminated site.
the bacterial consortium enriched with mixture of pesticides degraded all the three tested pesticides more efficiently as compared to the specific pesticide enriched cultures.
, in a multi-pesticide polluted site, it is always better to enrich the culture using the mixture of all the pesticides present in the site, which can degrade all the pesticides present at the site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to degrade pesticides using bacterial cultures.
the bacterial consortium enriched with all the possible pesticides present in a contaminated site can effectively biodegrade all the pesticides.
the bioremediation approach is effective and can be used for the removal of pesticides from soil and water.
